content: Do we have higher stacks as sheaves on sites valued in infinity groupoids?
Definitely not in mathlib: we do not have any serious theory of infinity-categories.
Just out of curiosity, do you have a particular model of infinity groupoid in mind, e.g., Kan complexes, or do you want a model-independent theory?

I am thinking as it is done in Lurie's Higher Topos Theory, so quasicategories. I see that Kan complexes and quasicategories as objects are in mathlib, but we seem to be lacking something like a quasicategory (in Type u+1) of quasicategories (in Type u).

We have the simplicial nerve, so we are not far from being able to define a reasonable quasicategory of quasicategories (or a quasicategory of Kan complex). But without much more infrastructure to actually manipulate it it would be a useless object.
I guess we are missing the theory of (co)cartesian fibrations?
What are people's thoughts about proving straightening-unstraightening following Cisinski--Nguyen?

Ken Lee said:

I guess we are missing the theory of (co)cartesian fibrations?

Among many other things, yes.

I am also on the side that if one wants to tackle straightening-unstraightening in lean (and any serious (∞,1)-category theory cannot avoid this equivalence at some point), the best way is to follow the paper you linked. As a prerequisite to that paper, one must first formalize the previous paper by Nguyen on covariant and contravariant homotopy theories, which itself relies on nontrivial existence results for cofibrantly generated model structures on presentable (1-)categories (see theorem 2.17 in that paper).

Another possible way for straightening-unstraightening from the definition via the simplicial nerve would be the proof in Kerodon. As far as I can recall, one of the key input in that proof is still the comparison between the mapping spaces of a simplicial nerve and the hom-simplicial set: https://kerodon.net/tag/01LE

About the technical existence result of model categories structures in the paper by Nguyen mentionned by @Robin Carlier, it depends on a certain variant of a theorem by Smith about model categories and locally presentable categories (theorem 2.20), and I have already formalized another variant (Theorem 1.7 at arxiv#math/0102087) at https://github.com/joelriou/mathlib4/blob/jriou_localization/Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/ModelCategory/Smith/Basic.lean
I did not check if there is an implication between both versions of Smith's theorem, but I wanted to mention that this "technology" should be available in mathlib in a not so distant future. (This is the reason I have developped the theory of accessible and locally presentable categories in mathlib...)
